name: Murata-blm18p
title: BLM series chip ferrite beads, 0201 to 1806, for signal lines and DC power lines
summary: The BLM family is a range of two-terminal monolithic chip ferrite beads placed in series with a signal or DC supply line; at high frequency their impedance is mostly resistive, and no ground connection is needed. Sizes run from 0.6 × 0.3 mm (0201) to 4.5 × 1.6 mm (1806). Sub-families are tuned for general use (A), sharp-impedance high-speed signals (B), digital interfaces (R), large DC current with low resistance (P, up to 6 A) and GHz-band suppression (H, E, G). The BLM18PG121SN1 is a 0603 large-current bead of 120 Ω ±25% at 100 MHz, rated 2000 mA with 0.05 Ω maximum DC resistance.

where.d1d2: first two digits of the three-digit impedance code, the significant figures
where.d3: third digit, the count of zeros after them

equations.note: Examples: 121 is 120 Ω, 102 is 1000 Ω, 050 is 5 Ω.

operation.text: Each bead behaves as an inductance in series with a frequency-dependent resistance. At low frequency the impedance is small and mostly reactive; as frequency rises the resistive part takes over. It sits in series with the line and needs no ground return, which makes it usable where a good ground is not available.
The A series builds impedance from comparatively low frequencies and suppresses noise over a broad band, roughly 30 MHz to several hundred MHz.
The B series has a sharp impedance characteristic that keeps attenuation of the signal waveform small. Many impedance values are offered so that one can be chosen to suit the signal frequency.
In the R series the resistance grows strongly already at lower frequencies. It therefore disturbs a digital waveform less at low frequency and damps ringing on the line.
The P series has low DC resistance for power lines; rated currents reach 6 A DC in the 0805, 1206 and 1806 sizes (BLM21PG220SN1, BLM31PG330SN1, BLM41PG600SN1).

The H, E and G types use an altered internal electrode layout that lowers stray capacitance, pushing the useful impedance range into the GHz band; their tables list impedance at 1 GHz as well as at 100 MHz. The E types are the low-DC-resistance versions.
The end electrodes have a nickel barrier layer, which gives the chips high resistance to soldering heat. The plating code S or T is tin, A is gold.
Rated currents marked * are subject to a derating of rated current.
